summary: Principal Enterprise AI Architect who designed and built Atlas, Fishbowl's internal agent harness: a sandboxed agent runtime with checkpointed dispatch, fail-closed step contracts, and human escalation; a trust boundary that caps every agent at its owner's permissions; MCP tool federation across 20+ connectors; a provider-agnostic inference layer with per-route cost tracking; queryable observability for every agent action; and accountable agent memory scored against run outcomes. The runtime, gateway, and streaming chat run in production. Applied AI Hackathon winner with deep frontend roots, including MicroFrontend solutions that unify disparate technology stacks.

roles.title: Principal Enterprise AI Architect
responsibilities: Designed and built Atlas, Fishbowl's internal AI agent platform and harness, as principal engineer in four months: runtime, trust boundary, MCP gateway, inference layer, observability, and memory. Delivered 1,854 commits across four core repositories, ~150K lines of TypeScript and Python, 506 test files, and 93 design specs, with TDD enforced throughout.

Built a harness-neutral agent runtime: a deterministic supervisor dispatches design, implement, review, fix, merge, and verify steps to pluggable harness adapters through a zod-validated contract that fails closed on prose or malformed output. Runs checkpoint to Postgres after every phase to survive pod loss, escalate to a human on needs_input, and pause in place or checkpoint out based on queue pressure.

Owned the trust boundary: an agent never exceeds its owner's grants, enforced once at the platform layer. Each run executes in a per-session Kubernetes sandbox with locked egress and short-lived, repo-scoped credentials from an identity broker that decides act-as-user, delegate, or deny. Per-turn act-as-user JWTs, Entra RBAC tool filtering, and read-only tool hints set per-thread approval modes.

Shipped an MCP gateway federating ~99 tools across 20+ connectors (Jira, Confluence, Slack, Microsoft 365, GitLab, Salesforce, Gong, Datadog, and more) behind a per-user credential vault. Its declarative connector framework cut the Salesforce connector to ~1KB, an 87% code reduction covered by 280+ tests, and keeps every tool a deterministic primitive with no agent loop inside.

Shipped the production chat runtime: a Vercel AI SDK tool-calling loop with step limits, SSE streaming with 15-second heartbeats that survive proxy idle cuts, and a 100K-character per-tool-result cap that bounds context. Routed all inference through one LiteLLM gateway with per-route cost accounting, and designed an advisor-model pattern with per-run cost telemetry to measure dollars per avoided human intervention.

Made every agent action a queryable structured event: a versioned telemetry envelope with trace-id propagation, tiered redaction plus a second secret scrub, and append-only audit mirrored to Datadog. Built a failure-triage agent that fires from the supervisor's failure chokepoint, investigates in a read-only sandbox, and returns an evidence-cited root cause with a copy-paste fix prompt.

Built accountable memory and multi-agent supervision, now running on dev. Memory pairs mem0 and pgvector with candidate and durable tiers, TTL horizons, one redaction chokepoint, and 150 ms fail-open recall. A 15-minute consolidation pass scores memories against run outcomes, promotes only facts corroborated across runs, and sends destructive changes to human review. Hermes steers workflows through a generic event bus.

Built the extension seams: versioned agent profiles and skills baked into sandbox images, merge-time review and TDD gates that agents must pass, and a chat transport factory that plugs new agents into the Tauri desktop and browser Studio. Themis orchestrates from Slack with model-driven intent and deterministic execution through RBAC-gated primitives, auto-proceeding only on high-confidence, reversible actions.
